findings.evidence: Erf/Basic.lean:49 is `public section` (no expose) for `Real.erf`/`Real.erfc`. Here `erf_def`, `erfc_def` and `faddeeva_def` already exist with `(rfl)`.
findings.fix: Use a plain `public section` and give consumers `_def` lemmas proved by `(rfl)` instead of exposed bodies.
findings.issue: `@[expose] public section` exposes the bodies of all seven definitions. Nothing downstream needs to unfold or compute them, and the sibling real file does not expose its bodies.

findings.evidence: grep finds no `fresnelC_def`, `fresnelS_def`, `fresnelTail_def` or `fresnelAux*_def`. The unfold sites are listed above.
findings.fix: Add `fresnelC_def`, `fresnelS_def`, `fresnelTail_def`, `fresnelAuxF_def` and `fresnelAuxG_def`, each `:= (rfl)`, and rewrite these proofs with the `_def` lemmas.
findings.issue: `fresnelC`, `fresnelS` (190), `fresnelTail` (194), `fresnelAuxF` (199) and `fresnelAuxG` (205) have no `_def` lemma. The file's own proofs unfold the bodies directly: `simp [fresnelC]` (283), `simp [fresnelS]` (286), `rw [fresnelC, fresnelC, …]` in `fresnelC_conj`, `unfold fresnelTail/fresnelAuxF/fresnelAuxG` (264, 270, 277), `simp [fresnelTail]` (314), `simp [fresnelAuxF]`/`[fresnelAuxG]` (323, 327). `differentiable_faddeeva` also uses `unfold faddeeva` (214) although `faddeeva_def` exists.

findings.evidence: HasPrimitives.lean:57 already hosts the `smul` form. Roadmap README.md:217: 'Entire functions as segment integrals. `erf`, `fresnelC`, `fresnelS`, `expIntegralEin`, …'.
findings.fix: Move both to `TauCeti/Analysis/Complex/HasPrimitives.lean`, next to `Differentiable.hasDerivAt_smul_integral_comp_mul`, as public lemmas (e.g. `Differentiable.hasDerivAt_integral_mul_comp_mul`).
findings.issue: `private hasDerivAt_integral_mul_comp_mul` is general infrastructure: its statement uses only Mathlib types (an entire `f : ℂ → ℂ`) and nothing specific to erf. `private integral_mul_comp_mul_neg` (72) is the same. The roadmap builds more entire functions as segment integrals (`expIntegralEin` and others), which will need both.

findings.evidence: Erf/Basic.lean:81-82 is `@[simp] theorem erf_neg` and Basic.lean:92-93 is `@[simp] theorem erfc_neg`.
findings.issue: `erf_neg`, `erfc_neg` (121), `fresnelC_neg` (289) and `fresnelS_neg` (293) are normal-form lemmas but carry no `@[simp]`. Their real counterparts do.

findings.evidence: Lines 270-273 and 277-280 add the lemmas as local hypotheses before `fun_prop`. The real file tags `continuous_erf` and `continuous_erfc` `@[fun_prop]` (Basic.lean:114, 138).
findings.fix: Tag the `differentiable_*` lemmas `@[fun_prop]` and drop the manual `have :=` steps.
findings.issue: None of the `differentiable_*` lemmas (98, 106, 213, 255, 259, 263, 269, 276) carries `@[fun_prop]`. As a result `differentiable_fresnelAuxF/G` need `have := differentiable_fresnelC; have := differentiable_fresnelS; fun_prop`, and `differentiable_faddeeva` composes by hand.

summary: Every definition body is exposed through `@[expose] public section`, and five definitions have no `_def` lemma, so proofs unfold them. Two general segment-integral lemmas are hidden as `private`, and the `simp`/`fun_prop` annotations are missing where the real-erf file sets the precedent.
